descriptions.preferred: This plant is the red-tinged form of 'Shigitatsu sawa', but with the lobes of the leaves slightly longer and more deeply separated. The leaves are seven lobed, sometimes The margins are wavy and have large, coarse, and sharp teeth. As the buds first open, the inner bud scales and new leaves are maroon. When fully opened, the typical leaf has quite dark veins on a light yellow-green background. The entire leaf is strongly overtoned with pink and red, however, which is the striking feature of this cultivar. This color holds very well into the summer, when the whole leaf darkens somewhat and develops a strong green tone within. This triple variegation of green, yellow, and pink is quite striking. The patterning can persist all summer when the tree is partly shaded, but is lost in full sunlight, the leaves becoming light green. 'Aka shigitatsu sawa' is not as strong growing as its green counterpart. It becomes a somewhat bushy tall plant up to 4 m tall and 5 m or so wide. It is hardy but not easy to propagate and is rather rare in nurseries and collections. It makes a very interesting specimen plant because of the unusual color form and combination. The ancient Japanese meaning of the name 'Aka shigitatsu sawa' is "red snipes over a winter marsh. " This cultivar has also been known under the names 'Beni shigitatsu sawa',

sources.title: 赤鸭立泽 Acer Palmatum 'Aka Shigitatsu Sawa'
sources.description: 赤鸭立泽是以火热的秋色闻名的，在庭院中呈现引人注目的橙色或红色。 春天迷人的乳白色叶子上带有一部分玫瑰粉，和绿色的叶脉互相衬托，更显春色柔和，色彩丰富使得小裂片掌状叶子具有很强的观赏性，纹理与 'Shigitatsu sawa' （鸭立泽）较为相似。 夏天转变为带有粉色的绿色，一年三个生长季节都带有红色调。 赤鸭立泽是一款 独特的、生长相当缓慢的 日本枫树 ， 非常适合小型景观的搭配， 成年树高约 3-4m 。

rhs.description: Bushy, deciduous tree about 4m tall, with deeply separated 7 lobed leaves 4-6cm long and 6-9cm wide, tapered to a sharp point and with wavy margins. Young leaves open crimson then dark veined, light yellow-green, overlaid with pink and red, holding this distinctive blend of colours into summer, later turning dark green, then red in autumn. Inconspicuous red-purple flowers in spring may be followed by winged, red fruits

attributes.hort_group_description: Acers in this matsumurae group are deeply divided to around three quarters of the leaf with coarsely-toothed edges and narrow, pointed lobes

care.cultivation: Grow in any moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in a sheltered position. Leaf colour is best in partial shade. Leaf scorch can be caused by lack of soil moisture or excessive exposure. Suits container cultivation but attention to watering is needed in dry spells during the growing season. Suitable for bonsai cultivation . See Japanese maples cultivation
care.pruning: Pruning group 1 from late autumn to midwinter only
care.propagation: Propagate by layering in autumn, grafting in late winter or softwood cuttings

resistance.pest: May be susceptible to Acer gall mite, aphids , caterpillars and horse chestnut scale
resistance.disease: May be susceptible to Verticillium wilt , acer leaf scorch and honey fungus

descriptions_zh.preferred: 本品种可视为 'Shigitatsu sawa' 的带红晕型，但叶裂片略长，分裂也更深。 叶片通常 7 裂，有时边缘起伏，并具较大、粗而尖锐的锯齿。 芽刚萌动时，内层芽鳞和新叶呈栗紫色。 叶片完全展开后，典型叶面表现为浅黄绿色底色上具较深色叶脉；但整片叶又强烈覆有粉色和红色调，这是本品种最显著的特征。 这种色彩能较好保持到夏季；入夏后整片叶颜色会略为加深，内部绿色调增强。 绿色、黄色与粉色三重斑彩效果十分醒目。 树体在半阴条件下，这种叶色斑纹可持续整个夏季；若处于全日照下，则会消失，叶片转为浅绿色。 'Aka shigitatsu sawa' 的生长势不如其绿色对应品种，最终形成较灌丛状的大型植株，高可达 4 米，冠幅约 5 米。 其耐寒，但繁殖不易，在苗圃和收藏中较为少见。 因其不寻常的色型与配色组合，是非常有趣的孤植观赏品种。 'Aka shigitatsu sawa' 这一名称的古日语含义为“冬日沼泽上方的红鹬”。 本品种也曾以 'Beni shigitatsu sawa'、

rhs_zh.description: 灌丛状落叶小乔木，高约 4 米；叶片深裂，7 裂，长 4-6 厘米、宽 6-9 厘米，裂片先端渐尖，叶缘呈波状。 嫩叶展开时呈深绯红色，随后显现深色叶脉、浅黄绿色底色，并覆有粉色与红色，这种独特的综合色彩可保持至夏季；之后叶色转为深绿色，秋季再转红。 春季开不显著的红紫色花，之后可能结带翅的红色果实

attributes.suggested_uses: 城市或庭院花园、乡村风或自然式花园
attributes.hort_group_description: 此 matsumurae 组的槭树，叶片深裂约达叶片的四分之三，叶缘具粗齿，裂片狭长且先端尖。

care.cultivation: 宜栽植于任何保水性好且排水良好的土壤中，选择避风位置。叶色在半阴环境下表现最佳。土壤缺水或暴露过强都可能导致叶灼。也适合容器栽培，但生长季遇干旱时需注意及时浇水。亦适于盆景栽培。参见 Japanese maples cultivation。
care.pruning: 修剪第 1 组：仅限在晚秋至仲冬期间进行。
care.propagation: 可于秋季行压条繁殖，于晚冬进行嫁接，或采用软枝扦插繁殖。

resistance.pest: 可能易受槭瘿螨、蚜虫、毛虫和七叶树介壳虫危害
resistance.disease: 可能易感 Verticillium wilt、槭树叶灼病和蜜环菌。
